decisions.note: Identical monitor stubs implement the same platform API in mutually exclusive backends; centralizing them would couple backend files that are expected to diverge.
The repeated buffer-state logging payload is coherent across subsystems and can be owned by one diagnostic helper while callers retain their context-specific prefixes.
The overlap sits in adjacent VM opcode cases whose operand decoding and dispatch boundaries must remain explicit even though their finish-set tails look alike.
The second member is a deliberately frozen historical source fixture under t/t4256, not a second maintained implementation that should share production code.
Each identical registration table belongs to a mutually exclusive allocator backend and resolves its function symbols inside that backend's compilation unit.
Six tests duplicate the same consumer-assignment lookup and assertions; one test helper can return the shared objects without hiding scenario-specific behavior.
These are distinct FloatHistogram fixtures already expressed as table rows; their repeated struct shape is the data contract rather than another abstraction boundary.
Four completion cases repeat execute/error/output assertions and vary only request arguments plus expected lines, which is a direct table-driven test boundary.
Debugger methods intentionally repeat lock/validity guards around different target operations; a helper cannot safely own each method's defer-scoped lock lifetime and return type.
The tests repeatedly create and close an httptest server before issuing the same request/assertion pattern; a scoped test helper can remove that setup without merging router scenarios.
The three four-line JUnit tearDown methods restore class-owned fields; introducing inheritance or a shared utility would cost more and couple otherwise unrelated test classes.
Two lifecycle cases in one test class rebuild the same large key set and assertion sequence; a parameterized assertion helper can preserve the lifecycle-specific counts.
Two checker test classes contain the same messageContaining factory and full Throwable condition implementation; a shared test utility is an exact extraction.
The package-private Internal classes are duplicated across package boundaries and Android/JRE source sets so each independently built artifact can use the helper without exporting it.
The multicast block overload is required on four transport implementations and differs at backend exception and address boundaries; the parallel interface implementations are deliberate.
Two puzzle test modules duplicate the complete operation-to-summary conversion; one assertion/normalization helper can serve both callers.
The overlap is an import list in two modules; Python imports cannot be extracted into a useful shared abstraction and the modules need their own names.
Four adjacent form-button tests repeat response construction and request assertions while varying markup and expected submitted fields, fitting a parameterized case helper.
The HTTP verb convenience functions differ only in the method constant and thin signature details, matching the rubric's canonical parameterization case.
The repeated assertions are checkpoints after different state transitions inside one report-behavior test; combining them would obscure the sequence rather than expose a reusable operation.
Five xcodebuild examples repeat a long expected command template and vary a bounded option set, so expected fragments and inputs can live in one table.
The multipart tests share body construction, mock environment creation, parsing, and core assertions; a helper can take the variant payload and expected fields.
Two fixture directories carry the exact same authored layout; under the rubric, fixture location does not excuse a reusable shared fixture or fixture-copy source.
The three public error pages are stock Rails application templates in a test fixture, with framework-generated styling and per-status payloads.
Adjacent invalid-name examples repeat Class.new plus the same error assertion and vary only the bad value and rendered message.
The integration tests repeatedly construct TestEnv and call assert_output with command arguments and expected text, a coherent parameterized harness boundary.
Ten integer writer methods repeat the same itoa buffer and write sequence and differ only by integer type, which can be expressed through a shared generic helper.
The printer test repeats a complete search-and-assert scenario for different context sizes; a table of builder settings and expected output is direct.
Four positional parsing cases share match construction and identical structural assertions while varying argument definitions and expected values.
The no-op run methods are small required command-trait implementations returning empty pipeline data; extracting them would not remove the required per-type methods.
Repeated markup blocks are intentionally parallel formatter fixtures for distinct colon-tag classifications; consolidating them would erase independent syntax cases.
Separate E2E fixture modules must preserve CJS, ESM, and resetModules loading contexts; their near-identical bodies are the controlled experiment.
The overlap is a handful of test-module imports, which cannot form a reusable runtime abstraction.
The shared storage setup appears in paired synchronous and asynchronous persistence specifications whose timing and hydration behavior are intentionally separate.
The v3 and v4 suites duplicate the same long email-validity corpus; sharing the test vectors preserves version-specific parsers while removing copied data.
Hundreds of repeated parameter tables come from generated API HTML and its generated docset copy, not maintained Swift source.
The shared documentation header is emitted across generated API pages and duplicated in the generated Dash docset.
The repeated breadcrumb markup is generated API documentation boilerplate across classes, protocols, structs, and docset copies.
Collection wrappers repeat the standard offsetForward/offsetBackward conformance surface over distinct Index semantics; a shared protocol layer would couple otherwise independent algorithms.
JoinedByCollection and JoinedByClosureCollection duplicate a substantial delegated Collection implementation and Index wrapper that can live behind one shared generic protocol/base layer.
Windows and Chain share unbounded index movement but intentionally differ in limitedBy boundary rules, so merging the detected whole fragments risks hiding collection-specific semantics.
Two CommandConfiguration initializers assign the same eleven fields and differ only by the experimental super-command value, which can delegate through one initializer.
Three global-option parsing tests share command execution and common assertions while varying arguments and a bounded expectation set.
Bare and Optional implement the exact same protocol update operation; a default protocol implementation can be shared while containers with different behavior override it.
The six minimal collection types deliberately expose different protocol capabilities and counters to test standard-library defaults; their parallel structure is the test design.
Four container types duplicate the same invariant-check control flow and dump-on-first-error behavior; a generic diagnostic wrapper can accept type-specific check and dump callbacks.
Two deque handles contain the same large closeGap algorithm with only wrapper annotations and mutability plumbing, a high-value shared implementation boundary.
These are progressive DocC tutorial snapshots of RecordMeetingView; each self-contained step intentionally carries forward earlier code.
CounterFeature copies are authored previous/current tutorial stages whose small deltas demonstrate the lesson; sharing them would defeat the documentation structure.
SyncUpsList variants are sequential DocC tutorial snapshots with intentionally evolving state and reducer behavior, not concurrent maintained implementations.
Seven named public log-level methods intentionally expose distinct API symbols and compile-time max-level guards while delegating the reusable work to _log.
The repeated _log calls are the small required bodies of level-specific public methods; the level constant and conditional compilation are the intended variant payload.
Level-specific convenience overloads already delegate to the fuller overload and must remain as separate public API entry points.
Three rule tests duplicate the exact conversion of removed triggering examples into a modified description and verification call; one test helper can take the base and removal list.
Four RulesFilter tests repeat the same rule universe and differ by exclusion category plus expected identifiers, fitting one table-driven test.
Analyze and Lint construct the same large options object from CommonOptions and vary only a small cache/stdin/rule tuple, suitable for a shared builder.
Runner and tester expose the same request construction/error-recording implementation; the runner can delegate to the tester's shared request helper.
Distinct public PeerMacro types are required for each HTTP attribute and already delegate behavior to HTTPMethodMacroUtilities; only unavoidable type shells remain.
The URL-encoded form tests repeatedly decode into User and assert the same common fields; a shared assertion helper can retain each encoding-specific input and extra checks.
